source.title: sleep2vec: Unified Cross-Modal Alignment for Heterogeneous Nocturnal Biosignals
source.authors: Weixuan Yuan; Zengrui Jin; Yichen Wang; Donglin Xie; Ziyi Ye; Chao Zhang; Xuesong Chen

page_placements.theme: Descriptive improvements across modalities do not establish a shared predictive law

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: Extends scaling analyses to nocturnal physiological signals, testing model-size, pre-training-data, and modality scaling. It does not fit or test the specific power-law relationships in the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports scaling trends for contrastive validation loss, downstream sleep-staging metrics, data fractions, and modality counts. It does not fit a power law or report exponents. The validation loss is contrastive loss, not held-out language-model cross-entropy; downstream metrics and modality-scaling results do not test the claim's specified power-law forms or compute-optimal allocation. Figure 7 loss values are shown only graphically.
record.test_reason: The paper calls its results 'scaling laws' for a contrastive sleep-biosignal model, but it fits no power law and reports no exponents. Loss is shown only graphically, for three model sizes spanning under one order of magnitude (63.5M–238.2M). Data scaling covers 25–100% of the corpus and is measured only on downstream metrics. These monotone trends cannot show whether the power-law form (V1/V5), extrapolation (V2) or compute-optimal allocation (V3) holds. Downstream gains are not tested for predictability from loss or scale (V6). It therefore discusses rather than tests any version, and the trends go under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors claim 'clear scaling laws' in modality diversity and model size, and also report gains from pretraining data, with diminishing returns for size and data. They fit no power laws.
record.recipe_differences: Physiological biosignal foundation model trained contrastively; evaluates scaling trends in downstream performance and contrastive validation loss, rather than language-model held-out cross-entropy power laws or compute-optimal allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports diminishing returns with increasing model size and pre-training data; it also reports that downstream results vary with modality count and evaluation cohort.

fits_no_version.finding: Contrastive validation loss falls, and sleep-staging accuracy rises with diminishing returns, from 63.5M to 238.2M parameters. No functional form is fitted.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In contrastive PSG biosignal pretraining, larger models give lower validation loss and better sleep staging over a ~4x size range.

fits_no_version.finding: Raising the pretraining data fraction from 25% to 100% raises SHHS Macro-F1 (77.2 to 79.5) and APPLES Macro-F1 (62.7 to 65.2). Gains diminish toward the full data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: More pretraining data improves downstream sleep staging in sleep2vec over a 4x data range.

record.problems: The parameter-scaling results are limited to three model sizes; Figure 7 reports contrastive validation loss graphically without numerical values or a fitted functional form. The study does not fit power laws or report exponents, and its scaling outcomes are not held-out language-model cross-entropy. No uncertainty estimates are given for the listed scaling results.
record.rows_left_out: The paper also reports parameter-scaling metrics other than accuracy (Cohen's Kappa, Macro-F1, sensitivity and specificity), modality-count ROC-AUC curves in Figure 5, and retrieval-accuracy trends in Figure 8 and Appendix A.6. These are not separately tabulated here because they are downstream or alignment measures rather than tests of the specified power-law loss forms; Figure 5 values are graphical and the text gives only the general trend.

untested.parts: No language-model cross-entropy; no power-law fit over orders of magnitude.
No extrapolation from small to large runs.
Depth and width co-vary with size (Table 5); there is no fixed-parameter shape comparison.
The power-law form in the biosignal modality is not fitted. There are only three sizes and four data fractions, and the loss is figure-only.
Downstream metrics rise with size and data, but there is no test of prediction from scale or loss.
No exponents or fitting choices to compare.

record.verdict_notes: The record set relation 'tests'/T3 but gave no labels and linked every row to 'none', which is inconsistent. This verdict changes the relation to 'discusses'. The 'scaling law' language is used loosely to mean monotone improvement. Retrieval accuracy also rises with data fraction (0.281 to 0.368, Tables 11–12), but this is not a version measure.

versions.untested_parts: No language-model held-out cross-entropy; no power-law fit for loss against parameters, tokens, or compute.
No extrapolation from small runs to larger runs.
No fixed-compute budget comparison or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
The study concerns physiological signals and reports scaling trends, but does not test whether the same power-law form holds in this modality or training regime.
No analysis of whether downstream performance is predictable from pretraining loss or scale.
No analysis of fitting choices, setup-dependent exponents, or departures from a single power law.

relation.reason: The study reports its own parameter- and data-scaling experiments on downstream performance, testing V6 within the measured range; it does not merely discuss scaling.

tranche.reason: Controlled pretraining-data scaling with fixed downstream fine-tuning yields monotonically improving downstream performance in a new biosignal setting (Tables 11–12), bearing directly on V6. V6 does not require a power-law fit.

source_check.notes: Row states are acceptable under their supplied version links of none, but r5–r12 jointly warrant V6 links and support within the tested range. No verdicts were listed; the lack of fitted power laws leaves V5 untested.

statements.correction: Pretraining fractions: 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%. SHHS Macro-F1 (%): 77.2, 77.9, 78.7, 79.5. APPLES Macro-F1 (%): 62.7, 63.0, 64.6, 65.2. Successive gains (percentage points): SHHS 0.7, 0.8, 0.8; APPLES 0.3, 1.6, 0.6. Diminishing returns asserted in Appendix A.5.2; no scaling function fitted.
statements.problem: The endpoints and absence of a fitted form are correct. The authors describe diminishing returns, but the tabulated Macro-F1 increments do not consistently diminish.
